purpose: Realistic multi-route mini-app. Planted business-logic vulnerabilities are co-located with benign and properly-gated sibling routes in the SAME modules, so the proof exercises in-file discrimination, not isolated single-pattern matching. Scanned .py files carry NO security-tell comments (a real PR would not annotate its own bugs); ground truth lives only in this non-.py manifest, which a `--ext=py` scan ignores.
note_on_lines: Line numbers point at the route decorator. They are advisory for human cross-check; the reachability runner asserts by route signature + file, not by line.

expected_vulnerable.why: Destructive op (deletes any user). The only dependency is get_session (a DB session, NOT auth). No get_current_user, no CurrentUser, no inline check. Unauthenticated caller can delete any account.

Privileged op (sets role; role=='admin' escalates is_superuser). Gated ONLY by CurrentUser (authenticated, NOT admin). No get_current_active_superuser, no is_superuser/role check. Any authenticated non-admin can promote anyone, including self.

Authenticated (CurrentUser), but session.get(Item, item_id) is keyed on a request-derived id with no owner_id filter and no post-fetch ownership check. Any authenticated user reads any item, including private ones owned by others.

expected_clear_controls.why: Public health check, non-sensitive, no destructive op. Benign no-auth route.
Authenticated update of OWN profile (current_user), no id from request.

expected_no_prefilter_match.why: Auth dependency definitions; no route decorator. Must NOT over-match the route-def regex.
Engine + session factory; no route decorator.
SQLModel table classes; no route decorator.
